content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Federated learning enables intrusion detection models to be trained and deployed on distributed edge nodes while reducing data transmission overhead by over 80%.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10526","field":"abstract","quote":"federated learning framework for distributed intrusion detection, wherein each edge node trains a local anomaly detection model"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Unsupervised anomaly detection using autoencoder-based neural networks trained on benign traffic can identify Modbus protocol attacks with detection rates exceeding 94% and false positive rates below 2%.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10523","field":"abstract","quote":"autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-10523","field":"abstract","quote":"detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%"}]},{"claim":3,"text":"Hybrid intrusion detection architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve better balance than purely deep-learning-based systems for SCADA networks.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10525","field":"abstract","quote":"hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance"}]}]}
